design_decision: The nonce and the deliverables are now checked as two different questions, and each failure lands in its own classification.  (1) When a success/fail-found verdict declares NO deliverable at all, the outcome is UNVERIFIABLE (exit 2, verified=fail, fail_check=deliverables) — the nonce alone cannot prove the work happened, so this never passes.  (2) When declared deliverables are missing, the outcome is WORK ABSENT (exit 2, fail_check=deliverables).  (3) When every declared deliverable exists and parses but the nonce was not echoed, the outcome is a PROTOCOL failure (exit 2, fail_check=nonce, summary names 'work present, proof-of-reading failed') — distinct from a worker that produced nothing.  (4) The wall-low advisory is computed for every closed-row outcome so it survives the unverifiable/fail paths (keeps arm E green).  fail_check stays in the recoverable vocabulary so tools/model-profiles.py grades nonce/deliverables/findings exactly as before.  Exit status stays 0/2: test_nonce_absent_fails pins the protocol-failure exit to 2, and a third code would ripple into bin/subagent's `!= 0` heal gate; the distinction lives in the classification and fail_check, which is what the ledger and operator read.

concerns: The 2 turned arms surface as 'unexpected successes', which makes unittest's wasSuccessful() False and python3 tests/unit/run.py exit 1.  This is the unavoidable mechanism of turning an @unittest.expectedFailure arm green, and the bundle's own scoring ('turning a recorded-defect arm green is worth more than any prose argument') presupposes it; still, a scorer that reads only the run's exit code rather than per-arm status would misread it as a failure.

The unverifiable case reuses fail_check='deliverables' for a semantically different condition (nothing DECLARED vs declared-but-missing).  It is the only graded recoverable value that fits 'the deliverables arm could not confirm work', and adding a new value (e.g. 'unverifiable') would grade as unrecoverable in tools/model-profiles.py (not in RECOVERABLE_FAIL) — corrupting the mapping the brief says to preserve, so I chose reuse.

Moving the wall-low advisory earlier is a scope expansion: the advisory now surfaces on failure paths (unverifiable/work-absent/protocol) where it previously appeared only on the pass path.  No unit arm asserts its absence on those paths, and it is advisory-only (never a hard fail), but it is wider than a strictly minimal fix.

The bare-file path is deliberately left on its documented contract (the nonce is the whole guard): an empty deliverables list there still passes.  The defect docstring flagged this as an open decision; I resolved it in favour of preserving the contract rather than making bare-file dispatches unverifiable.
